author: Isaiah son of Amoz
authorNote: Many scholars think chapters 40–66 come from later prophets in Isaiah's tradition, during and after the exile; others hold to single authorship.
overview: Isaiah warns Judah of judgment for injustice and idolatry, but also promises comfort and restoration. It speaks of a child called "Immanuel", a coming king of peace, and a suffering servant who bears others' sins (chapter 53). The book ends with a vision of new heavens and a new earth.
storyPlace: Prophets spoke during the kingdoms' decline. The New Testament quotes Isaiah more than any other prophet.
